I added all three improvements to the existing crawler in the image. All 53 tests pass: the 16 that were already there and 37 new ones. I ran the suite several times and got the same result each time.

One change to what was there: the existing test class was in the `SurveyCrawler` category, so I moved it to `SurveyCrawler-Tests`.

## Design
- **Repeated commands:** the crawler remembers the last `a`/`t`/`h`/`g` it ran in the current sequence. A digit runs that command digit + 2 more times, then clears it. So a digit at the start, a second digit in a row, or a digit after `(`, `)` or an invalid command raises an error.
- **Sonar and ground:** there's a new class `SimulatedSonar` that maps positions to ground types; any position not in the map is firm sand. The old `at:facing:` still works and uses an all-firm-sand sonar; `at:facing:sonar:` lets you pass one in. Each ground type (`FirmSandGround`, `BoulderGround`, `SiltGround`) decides what happens to the crawler:
  - **Firm sand:** the crawler moves normally.
  - **Boulder:** raises an error. Moves check the ground at the destination; turns check the ground the crawler is standing on.
  - **Silt:** the crawler slides `Random nextInteger: 10` cells in the direction it was moving; turning works normally. The random source can be swapped out, so tests use a stub that always slides a fixed distance.
- **Guarded runs:** the crawler has two modes, normal and guarded (`CrawlerNormalRun`, `CrawlerGuardedRun`), so it doesn't need `if` checks on a flag.
  - Guarded mode wraps each command in `on: Error do:`. On any error it switches back to normal mode, undoes the moves and `pass`es the exception on.
  - Every move and turn in a guarded run saves its opposite action (move back the same distance, or turn the other way). Undoing runs these in reverse order.
  - Guarded mode also raises the silt error and the error for starting a guarded run inside another. At the end of the sequence it undoes the moves and raises the "not finished" error.

## Choices where the spec was silent
- **Silt in a guarded run:** the error is raised before moving, so there's no slide to undo.
- **Undoing:** reverse moves don't check the sonar. They only go back over cells the crawler just came from, and a guarded run never lands on silt, so those cells are firm sand.
- **Retreating onto silt:** the crawler keeps sliding backwards.
- **Sliding:** it doesn't check the cells it slides over, so it can end up on a boulder.
- **Errors outside a guarded run:** moves already made are kept, as before.
- **Other new errors:**
  - A `)` without a matching `(` raises its own error.
  - A repetition doesn't carry over from one `process:` call to the next.
  - After any error the crawler is back in normal mode and can take new commands.

The new tests cover these cases, plus the examples from the spec: `'a0'`, a boulder at `1@3` and at `1@2`, silt ending between `1@3` and `1@12`, `'(aa)'`, `'aha(aagt3)aa(ht)'`, `'aa(aa(ht)a)'` and `'a(aa'`.
